## Why Gerridae? {background-color="#0B3D91" background-opacity="0.9"}


```{r setup}
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(patchwork)
library(viridis)
library(scales)
library(ggridges)
library(treemapify)
library(ggtext)
library(xgboost)
library(caret)

# ── Presentation palette ──────────────────────────────────────
pal <- list(
  ocean   = "#0B3D91",
  fresh   = "#2E8B57",
  accent  = "#FF6F00",
  light   = "#F5F5F5",
  dark    = "#1A1A2E",
  grid    = c("#0B3D91", "#2E8B57", "#FF6F00", "#E53935",
              "#8E24AA", "#00ACC1", "#FFB300", "#43A047")
)

habitat_colours <- c(
  "oceanic"    = "#0B3D91",
  "freshwater" = "#2E8B57"
)

# ── Global ggplot theme ───────────────────────────────────────
theme_xfm <- function(base_size = 18) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) %+replace%
    theme(
      text             = element_text(family = "sans", colour = pal$dark),
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.3),
                                      hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = "grey40", hjust = 0,
                                      margin = margin(b = 15)),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(0.9))
    )
}
theme_set(theme_xfm())

# ── Helper functions ──────────────────────────────────────────
safe_median <- function(x, ...) stats::median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
safe_mean   <- function(x, ...) base::mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── Load and prepare real dataset ─────────────────────────────
df_all_raw <- read.csv("DATA/xrf_summary_statistics_merged.csv") |>
  rename(mean_conc = mean)

# Filter: intact only, oceanic vs freshwater only
df_all <- df_all_raw |>
  filter(Condition == "intact",
         Lifestyle %in% c("oceanic", "freshwater")) |>
  mutate(habitat = if_else(Lifestyle == "oceanic", "Oceanic", "Freshwater"))

all_elements <- sort(unique(df_all$Element))
all_samples  <- unique(df_all$Sample)
```

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

### A natural experiment in elemental adaptation

- **Gerridae** (water striders) colonised marine habitats **independently multiple times**
- Oceanic genus *Halobates* — the **only truly pelagic insects**
- Freshwater genera (*Metrocoris*, *Ventidius*) occupy chemically distinct niches
- **Question:** How does habitat chemistry reshape the whole-body elemental fingerprint?

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

![](img/gerridae_habitat_comparison.png){fig-alt="Side-by-side: oceanic Halobates on wave surface vs freshwater Gerris on pond" width="100%"}

:::

::::

## Research objectives {.smaller}

<br>

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## 🎯 Three integrated goals

**1. Map** — Acquire high-resolution synchrotron XFM elemental maps of whole Gerridae specimens from oceanic and freshwater habitats.

**2. Quantify** — Extract robust per-element descriptive statistics and compare distributions across habitats.

**3. Explain** — Train a gradient-boosted classifier (XGBoost) on the elemental profiles and interpret predictions with SHAP values to identify the most discriminative elements.
:::

<br>

```{r objectives-flow, fig.width=16, fig.height=5}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

flow <- tibble(
  step  = factor(c("Specimen\npreparation", "Synchrotron\nXFM", "Spectral\nfitting", 
                    "Feature\nextraction", "XGBoost\nclassifier", "SHAP\ninterpretation"),
                 levels = c("Specimen\npreparation", "Synchrotron\nXFM", "Spectral\nfitting",
                            "Feature\nextraction", "XGBoost\nclassifier", "SHAP\ninterpretation")),
  x     = 1:6,
  col   = c(pal$dark, pal$ocean, pal$ocean, pal$fresh, pal$accent, pal$accent)
)

ggplot(flow, aes(x, y = 0)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x + 0.42, xend = x + 0.58, y = 0, yend = 0),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.35, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               colour = "grey50", linewidth = 1.2,
               data = flow |> filter(x < 6)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = I(col)), shape = 21, size = 52,
             colour = "grey30", stroke = 1.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = step), size = 5.5, colour = "white", fontface = "bold",
            lineheight = 0.85) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.0, 6.9)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.8, 0.8)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10))
```

```{r specimen-table}

df_all |>

  )
```

<br>

- Specimens preserved in **ethanol → air-dried → mounted on Ultralene**
- No chemical fixation to avoid elemental contamination
- Whole-body mounts (dorsal orientation)
- Only **intact** specimens included (*n* = 13)

## Per-element statistics overview {.smaller .scrollable}

```{r stats-table}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

# ── Compute stats for each habitat separately ────────────────
compute_stats <- function(data, hab_label) {
  data |>
    filter(habitat == hab_label) |>
    group_by(Element) |>
    summarise(
      pct_nz  = safe_mean(pct_nz),
      mean_c  = safe_mean(mean_conc),
      median_c = safe_mean(median),
      p99_c   = safe_mean(p99),
      skew    = safe_mean(p99 / mean_conc),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

stats_fw  <- compute_stats(df_all, "Freshwater")
stats_oc  <- compute_stats(df_all, "Oceanic")

# ── Join side-by-side ─────────────────────────────────────────
stats_wide <- stats_fw |>
  rename(fw_pct = pct_nz, fw_mean = mean_c, fw_median = median_c,
         fw_p99 = p99_c, fw_skew = skew) |>
  left_join(
    stats_oc |>
      rename(oc_pct = pct_nz, oc_mean = mean_c, oc_median = median_c,
             oc_p99 = p99_c, oc_skew = skew),
    by = "Element"
  ) |>
  mutate(fold_delta = oc_mean / fw_mean) |>
  arrange(desc(fold_delta))

# ── Build GT table ────────────────────────────────────────────
stats_wide |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    Element    = "Element",
    fw_pct     = "% NZ",
    fw_mean    = "Mean",
    fw_median  = "Median",
    fw_p99     = "P99",
    fw_skew    = "Skew",
    oc_pct     = "% NZ",
    oc_mean    = "Mean",
    oc_median  = "Median",
    oc_p99     = "P99",
    oc_skew    = "Skew",
    fold_delta = "Fold Δ"
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = md("🌿 **Freshwater** (n = 3)"),
              columns = starts_with("fw_")) |>
  tab_spanner(label = md("🌊 **Oceanic** (n = 10)"),
              columns = starts_with("oc_")) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(fw_pct, oc_pct), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(fw_mean, fw_median, fw_p99,
                         oc_mean, oc_median, oc_p99), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(fw_skew, oc_skew), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = fold_delta, decimals = 1) |>
  data_color(
    columns = fw_median,
    palette = c("#E8F5E9", "#1B5E20"),
    domain  = c(0, max(c(stats_wide$fw_median, stats_wide$oc_median), na.rm = TRUE))
  ) |>
  data_color(
    columns = oc_median,
    palette = c("#E3F2FD", "#0D47A1"),
    domain  = c(0, max(c(stats_wide$fw_median, stats_wide$oc_median), na.rm = TRUE))
  ) |>
  data_color(
    columns = fold_delta,
    palette = c("#FFCDD2", "#FFFFFF", "#C8E6C9"),
    domain  = c(0, max(stats_wide$fold_delta, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_fill(color = "#E8F5E9")),
    locations = cells_column_spanners(spanners = "🌿 **Freshwater** (n = 3)")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(cell_fill(color = "#E3F2FD")),
    locations = cells_column_spanners(spanners = "🌊 **Oceanic** (n = 10)")
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title    = md("**Per-element statistics: Freshwater vs Oceanic**"),
    subtitle = md("Intact specimens only · concentrations in ng cm⁻² · sorted by fold-change")
  ) |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size        = px(16),
    column_labels.font.size = px(17),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold"
  )
```

## Oceanic vs freshwater: fold-change

```{r fold-change, fig.width=16, fig.height=8}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

fc_data <- df_all |>
  group_by(habitat, Element) |>
  summarise(grp_mean = safe_mean(mean_conc), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = habitat, values_from = grp_mean) |>
  mutate(
    log2_fc   = log2(Oceanic / Freshwater),
    direction = if_else(log2_fc > 0, "Enriched in oceanic", "Enriched in freshwater"),
    Element   = fct_reorder(Element, log2_fc)
  )

ggplot(fc_data, aes(x = log2_fc, y = Element, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.8, colour = pal$dark) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f×", 2^abs(log2_fc)),
                hjust = if_else(log2_fc > 0, -0.1, 1.1)),
            size = 4.5, colour = pal$dark) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Enriched in oceanic" = pal$ocean,
                                "Enriched in freshwater" = pal$fresh),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "Log₂ fold-change: oceanic relative to freshwater",
    subtitle = "Positive = higher in oceanic specimens · intact samples only",
    x = expression(log[2]~"fold-change"),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_xfm(base_size = 20) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Feature size distribution (P75 thresholding) {.smaller}

```{r feature-size, fig.width=16, fig.height=8}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

# ── Panel 1: P99/Mean heterogeneity ratio ─────────────────────
hetero_data <- df_all |>
  filter(mean_conc > 0) |>
  mutate(p99_mean_ratio = p99 / mean_conc) |>
  group_by(Lifestyle, Element) |>
  summarise(ratio_mean = safe_mean(p99_mean_ratio), .groups = "drop")

p_hetero <- ggplot(hetero_data,
                   aes(x = reorder(Element, ratio_mean), y = ratio_mean,
                       fill = Lifestyle)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = habitat_colours, name = "Habitat") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Spatial heterogeneity (P99 / Mean)",
       subtitle = "Higher = hotspot-concentrated",
       x = NULL, y = "P99 / Mean ratio") +
  theme_xfm(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# ── Panel 2: % specimens above P75 ────────────────────────────
p75_data <- df_all |>
  group_by(Element) |>
  mutate(p75_threshold = quantile(mean_conc, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(above_p75 = mean_conc > p75_threshold) |>
  group_by(Lifestyle, Element) |>
  summarise(pct_above = safe_mean(above_p75) * 100, .groups = "drop")

p_p75 <- ggplot(p75_data,
                aes(x = reorder(Element, pct_above), y = pct_above,
                    fill = Lifestyle)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = habitat_colours, name = "Habitat") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "% specimens above P75 threshold",
       subtitle = "Cross-habitat 75th percentile",
       x = NULL, y = "% above P75") +
  theme_xfm(base_size = 16) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

(p_hetero | p_p75) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Concentration heterogeneity and P75 thresholding",
    subtitle = "Intact specimens only · oceanic vs freshwater",
    theme = theme_xfm(base_size = 18)
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

<!-- ============================================================
     SLIDE 13 — XGBoost + SHAP
     ============================================================ -->

## Explainable AI: XGBoost classification {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

```{r xgboost-train, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
#| echo: false

# ── Prepare data for XGBoost ─────────────────────────────────
model_data <- df_all |>
  select(Sample, habitat, Element, mean_conc) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Element, values_from = mean_conc) |>
  mutate(label = if_else(habitat == "Oceanic", 1L, 0L))

feature_names <- setdiff(names(model_data), c("Sample", "habitat", "label"))

X_mat <- model_data |>
  select(all_of(feature_names)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ log1p(.x))) |>
  as.matrix()

y_vec <- model_data$label

# ── Balanced sample weights ───────────────────────────────────
n_oc <- sum(y_vec == 1)
n_fw <- sum(y_vec == 0)
w_vec <- if_else(y_vec == 1, 1.0, n_oc / n_fw)

# ── Leave-one-out cross-validation ────────────────────────────
n <- nrow(X_mat)
loo_preds <- numeric(n)

for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  dtrain_i <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_mat[-i, , drop = FALSE],
                           label = y_vec[-i], weight = w_vec[-i])
  dtest_i  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_mat[i, , drop = FALSE])
  
  model_i <- xgb.train(
    params = list(
      objective        = "binary:logistic",
      eval_metric      = "logloss",
      max_depth        = 3,
      eta              = 0.1,
      alpha            = 1,
      lambda           = 5,
      colsample_bytree = 0.7,
      subsample        = 0.8
    ),
    data    = dtrain_i,
    nrounds = 100,
    verbose = 0
  )
  loo_preds[i] <- predict(model_i, dtest_i)
}

loo_class <- if_else(loo_preds > 0.5, 1L, 0L)
loo_accuracy <- safe_mean(loo_class == y_vec) * 100

roc_obj <- pROC::roc(y_vec, loo_preds, quiet = TRUE)
loo_auc <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))

# ── Train final model on all data ─────────────────────────────
dtrain_full <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_mat, label = y_vec, weight = w_vec)

final_model <- xgb.train(
  params = list(
    objective        = "binary:logistic",
    eval_metric      = "logloss",
    max_depth        = 3,
    eta              = 0.1,
    alpha            = 1,
    lambda           = 5,
    colsample_bytree = 0.7,
    subsample        = 0.8
  ),
  data    = dtrain_full,
  nrounds = 100,
  verbose = 0
)

# ── Feature importance (gain) ─────────────────────────────────
imp <- xgb.importance(feature_names = feature_names, model = final_model)

imp |>
  mutate(Feature = fct_reorder(Feature, Gain)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Gain, y = Feature)) +
  geom_col(fill = pal$ocean, width = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "XGBoost feature importance (Gain)",
    subtitle = "Oceanic vs freshwater · intact specimens",
    x = "Gain", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_xfm(base_size = 16)
```

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

### Model performance

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Accuracy (LOO-CV) | **`r sprintf("%.0f", loo_accuracy)` %** |
| AUC-ROC | **`r sprintf("%.2f", loo_auc)`** |
| Samples | `r n` (10 oceanic, 3 freshwater) |
| Features | `r length(feature_names)` elements (log₁p) |
| Weights | Balanced (inverse frequency) |

<br>

### Key insights

- **Ca** dominates gain — strongest single discriminator
- **Br, Mn** provide complementary separation
- Model uses only a **subset** of 16 elements
- Fully interpretable via SHAP (next slide)

:::

::::



<!-- ============================================================
     SLIDE 14 — SHAP BEESWARM
     ============================================================ -->

## SHAP beeswarm: feature-value interactions

```{r shap-beeswarm, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

# ── TreeSHAP contributions ────────────────────────────────────
shap_raw <- predict(final_model, dtrain_full, predcontrib = TRUE)
shap_mat <- shap_raw[, 1:length(feature_names)]
colnames(shap_mat) <- feature_names

# ── Filter to features with non-zero SHAP ─────────────────────
shap_abs_mean <- colMeans(abs(shap_mat))
active_feats  <- names(shap_abs_mean[shap_abs_mean > 1e-6])

if (length(active_feats) == 0) active_feats <- feature_names[1:4]

feat_order <- names(sort(shap_abs_mean[active_feats]))

beeswarm_df <- shap_mat[, active_feats, drop = FALSE] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(sample_idx = row_number()) |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_idx, names_to = "Feature", values_to = "shap_value") |>
  left_join(
    X_mat[, active_feats, drop = FALSE] |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      mutate(sample_idx = row_number()) |>
      pivot_longer(-sample_idx, names_to = "Feature", values_to = "feature_value"),
    by = c("sample_idx", "Feature")
  ) |>
  group_by(Feature) |>
  mutate(
    feat_scaled = (feature_value - min(feature_value)) /
                  (max(feature_value) - min(feature_value) + 1e-10)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Feature = factor(Feature, levels = feat_order))

ggplot(beeswarm_df, aes(x = shap_value, y = Feature, colour = feat_scaled)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.25, width = 0, size = 4.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#B2182B",
                         midpoint = 0.5, name = "Feature value\n(scaled)",
                         labels = c("Low", "", "High"),
                         breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.6, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(
    title    = "TreeSHAP beeswarm plot",
    subtitle = "Each dot = one specimen · colour = element concentration · x = impact on prediction",
    x = "SHAP value (→ Oceanic)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_xfm(base_size = 18) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.height = unit(2, "cm"))
```



<!-- ============================================================
     SLIDE 15 — BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
     ============================================================ -->

## Biological interpretation {.smaller .dark background-color="#1A1A2E"}


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### 🌊 Oceanic enrichment

* **Sr** (~11× higher) — seawater Sr incorporated into cuticle
* **Br** (~6× higher) — marine halide bioaccumulation
* **Ca** (~3× higher) — enhanced cuticular mineralisation
* **Zn, Se** — moderately elevated, metalloprotein pools

### 🌿 Freshwater enrichment

* **Mn** (~2× higher) — reflects freshwater trace-metal chemistry
* **Cu** (~1.7× higher) — dietary or environmental source
* **K** (~1.6× higher) — osmoregulatory differences

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### ⚖️ Habitat-invariant elements

* **Se, As, Ni** — fold-change ≈ 1, homeostatic regulation
* ** Essential trace elements maintained regardless of environment

### 🤖 XAI confirmation

* **XGBoost** selects only 3–4 elements from 16 available
* **SHAP** confirms monotonic Ca/Br → oceanic, Mn → freshwater
* **Sparse model** = robust, interpretable signature

:::

::::

::: {.callout-important icon=false}
## 🔬 Hypothesis for future work

Oceanic *Halobates* show **Sr-enriched cuticular mineralisation** as a potential structural adaptation to wave-dominated habitats. XANES at the Sr K-edge and Ca K-edge could confirm whether Sr substitutes into a carbonate or phosphate lattice.
:::





<!-- ============================================================
     SLIDE 16 — METHODOLOGICAL CONSIDERATIONS
     ============================================================ -->

## Methodological considerations

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Strengths

✅ Non-destructive, whole-specimen mapping at µm resolution

✅ Simultaneous multi-element detection (16 elements)

✅ Quantitative areal densities via fundamental parameters

✅ TreeSHAP provides exact, per-specimen explanations

✅ Reproducible pipeline: R + Quarto + version control

✅ Balanced sample weights handle class imbalance

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Limitations & future directions

⚠️ Small sample size (*n* = 13) — expand to more species

⚠️ Class imbalance (10 oceanic vs 3 freshwater)

⚠️ 2D projection — consider confocal XFM for depth info

⚠️ No chemical speciation — XANES at Ca, Sr, Fe edges

⚠️ Hollow specimens excluded — compare preservation states

⚠️ Nymph vs adult differences merit investigation (MIC6–8)

⚠️ Body-size confounding — mass-normalised comparison needed

:::

::::

## Iterative reporting: element exclusion {.smaller}

```{r exclusion-demo, fig.width=16, fig.height=7}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show exclusion workflow code"

# ── User-selectable exclusion vector ──────────────────────────
elements_to_exclude <- c("CdL", "PbL")   # ← edit as needed

df_filtered <- df_all |>
  filter(!Element %in% elements_to_exclude)

fc_filtered <- df_filtered |>
  group_by(habitat, Element) |>
  summarise(grp_mean = safe_mean(mean_conc), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = habitat, values_from = grp_mean) |>
  mutate(
    log2_fc   = log2(Oceanic / Freshwater),
    direction = if_else(log2_fc > 0, "Enriched in oceanic", "Enriched in freshwater"),
    Element   = fct_reorder(Element, log2_fc)
  )

ggplot(fc_filtered, aes(x = log2_fc, y = Element, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.8, colour = pal$dark) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f×", 2^abs(log2_fc)),
                hjust = if_else(log2_fc > 0, -0.1, 1.1)),
            size = 4.5, colour = pal$dark) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Enriched in oceanic" = pal$ocean,
                                "Enriched in freshwater" = pal$fresh),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = glue::glue("Fold-change after excluding: {paste(elements_to_exclude, collapse = ', ')}"),
    subtitle = "Second-iteration analysis — remaining elements only",
    x = expression(log[2]~"fold-change"),
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_xfm(base_size = 20) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```



<!-- ============================================================
     SLIDE 18 — CONCLUSIONS
     ============================================================ -->

## Conclusions {background-color="#0B3D91" background-opacity="0.85" style="color: #F5F5F5;"}

<br>

### Key findings

:::{style="font-size: 1.15em; line-height: 1.8;"}

**1.** Synchrotron XFM resolves distinct elemental fingerprints between oceanic and freshwater Gerridae at 2 µm resolution across 16 elements.

**2.** Strontium (~11×), bromine (~6×), and calcium (~3×) are the **most discriminative elements** — pointing to enhanced cuticular mineralisation in oceanic species.

**3.** XGBoost with TreeSHAP provides **transparent, interpretable classification** using only 3–4 of 16 available elements.

**4.** Manganese and copper are enriched in freshwater specimens, while selenium and arsenic are habitat-invariant.

**5.** P75 thresholding reveals habitat-dependent spatial organisation of element-rich regions.

:::

## Backup: inter-element correlation {visibility="uncounted"}

```{r correlation, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

cor_mat <- df_all |>
  select(Sample, Element, mean_conc) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Element, values_from = mean_conc) |>
  select(-Sample) |>
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

# ── Hierarchical clustering for element order ─────────────────
hc <- hclust(as.dist(1 - cor_mat), method = "ward.D2")
el_order <- hc$labels[hc$order]

cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) |>
  rename(el1 = Var1, el2 = Var2, r = Freq) |>
  mutate(
    el1 = factor(el1, levels = el_order),
    el2 = factor(el2, levels = el_order)
  )

ggplot(cor_long, aes(el1, el2, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3.5, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Pearson r") +
  labs(title = "Inter-element correlation matrix (hierarchically clustered)",
       subtitle = "Intact specimens · oceanic + freshwater · Ward's D2 linkage",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_xfm(base_size = 16) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
